measurements.raw_composition: 3D printed CSSE (vertically aligned LLZTO in PEO/LiTFSI)
material_definitions: Composite solid-state electrolytes (CSSEs) consisting of polymers and ceramic fillers were fabricated using direct ink writing 3D printing.
The ceramic filler used is garnet-type Li6.4La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 (LLZTO).
The polymer matrix consists of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI).
The 3D printing method allows for the vertical alignment of the ceramic filler to enhance ionic transport.
The resulting CSSE with vertically aligned fillers is compared against a CSSE with randomly distributed fillers.
Composite solid-state electrolytes (CSSEs) consisting of polymers and ceramic fillers were fabricated using direct ink writing 3D printing.
The ceramic filler used is garnet-type Li6.4La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 (LLZTO).
The polymer matrix consists of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI).
The 3D printing method allows for the vertical alignment of the ceramic filler to enhance ionic transport.
The resulting CSSE with vertically aligned fillers is compared against a CSSE with randomly distributed fillers.
The LISICON materials Li3P1-xVxO4, Li3+xV1-xGexO4, and Li3+xP1-xGexO4 (x = 0 to 1) were confirmed as phase pure via X-ray powder diffraction.
Stoichiometric compounds Li3PO4 and Li4GeO4 exhibit low lithium-ion conductivities with high activation energies of approximately 1.1 eV.
Aliovalent substitution of Ge4+ into Li3PO4 or Li3VO4 creates partial lithium occupancy, leading to a conductivity increase of 4-5 orders of magnitude.
The unit cell volumes of the Li3P1-xVxO4 and Li3+xP1-xGexO4 series increase with Ge and V content, reflecting larger ionic sizes compared to phosphorus.
The relationship between the pre-exponential factor and activation energy in these LISICONs follows the Meyer-Neldel rule, linked to multi-excitation entropy.
